body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending. Claims 1, 8, and 15 are independent.

Applicant amends claims 1-20 solely to improve their form and expedite prosecution. No new matter is added. Applicant does not concede patentability of the subject matter encompassed by the claims before this amendment over the art cited by the Examiner. Applicant reserves the right to pursue claims in one or more continuing applications, including additional claims and claims capturing the subject matter encompassed by the claims before this amendment. At least 49 of the Specification supports this amendment.
Claims 1-20 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,801,832.
Without conceding the propriety of this rejection, Applicant submits a terminal disclaimer with this Response.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as allegedly anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Pub. No. 2019/0137290 to Levy et al. (LEVY). Applicant traverses this rejection.
Page 8 of 11
A proper rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 requires that a single reference teach every aspect of the claimed invention. Any feature not directly taught must be inherently present. (See MPEP 2131.)
Without conceding the propriety of this rejection, Applicant amends the claims solely to expedite prosecution.
For example, claim 1 recites:
detecting by a processing node that a transport has parked at a first location of an event;
determine by the processing node a pickup location where the

transport is to be located at a pickup time, wherein the pickup location and the pickup time are based on a time of a conclusion of the event obtained from a device of an occupant of the transport; and

in response to the processing node receiving a modified pickup time for the conclusion of the event from the device, causing by the processing node the transport to move to a second location intermediate between the first location and the pickup location at the modified pickup time.
LEVY does not anticipate the above-identified features of claim 1. Accordingly, the Applicant requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw this rejection of claim 1.

Independent claims 8 and 15 now recite features similar to (yet possibly of different scope than) features described above concerning claim 1. Therefore, the Applicant submits that LEVY does not anticipate claims 8 and 15 for at least reasons similar to those given above regarding claim 1. Accordingly, the Applicant requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw this rejection of claims 8 and 15.
Page 9 of 11

Applicant submits that LEVY does not anticipate the dependent claims for at least the reasons given above concerning claims 1, 8, and 15, respectively. Accordingly, the Applicant requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw this rejection of these claims. Moreover, the Applicant submits that these claims are patentable for their reasons.
Page 10 of 11
The Applicant submits that the claims are in condition for allowance.

The Applicant submits that this response overcomes the Examiner's rejections. The Applicant's silence as to assertions or requirements in the Office Action that may apply to such assertions (e.g., whether a reference constitutes prior art, reasons to modify a reference or to combine references, assertions as to dependent claims, allegations of Official Notice, etc.) is not a concession by the Applicant that such assertions are accurate or such requirements have been met. Accordingly, the Applicant reserves the right to dispute such assertions.
If the Examiner believes a telephone conference would expedite the prosecution of this application, please telephone Michael Brooke at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted,
